Q: Getting Node Module Error (Cannot find module) A:

This is probably an issue with the current working directory that Windows Task Scheduler uses when it executes its action (in this case node).

Edit the value of 'Start In (optional)' in the 'Edit Action' dialog in Windows Task scheduler for your task and set it to the path of where your node_modules folder and your other source files are located.

Q: External Control of File Name or Path Veracode scanning issue A:

It is mainly because of the filepath,filestream or stream writer. Make sure that you validate the path with your input. Veracode thinks that a hacker can add a path say windows/importantfile and would try to get access to that folder.

If you are not validating your path with input this flaw may come up with veracode.

Please see the link for more information. Veracode directory traversal Issue c#

Q: Change color of Windows 11 taskbar search popup with C# (WinUI, .NET 10) A:

There is no way to programmatically change the background/accent color of the Windows 11 taskbar Search box (SearchHost.exe) in a WinUI 3/C# app via any supported Windows APIs.

DwmSetWindowAttribute won’t work here because although it allows you to change some of the DWM-related window attributes like borders, captions, and dark mode, the Search box itself is managed by the Windows shell and is not available for third-party customization.

If your app needs to pass WACK/Microsoft Store validation, do not attempt to interfere with the SearchHost.exe in any way using injection, subclassing, hooking, private registry keys, memory modifications, etc.

The only supported approach here is to leave the control of the Search appearance to Windows through the Personalization/Accent Color settings. Here’s how you can launch the corresponding settings page from your app:

using System;
using Windows.System;

await Launcher.LaunchUriAsync(
    new Uri("ms-settings:personalization-colors"));

The user can then configure:

Settings → Personalization → Colors → Accent color

The colored flyout for the search displayed in the example above would then be due to Windows theming/personalization rather than being caused by an application invoking the public API of SearchHost.exe.

Q: Amazon SES: BadRequestException and HTTP Body: {"message":null} A:

{"message":null} doesn't mean the message body is null, it means there is no specific error message. Were it not to be null, I would have expected something like {"message":"Source must not be null"}

You should look at the response's Reason/Status phrase (which may or may not be returned) and I would expect that to be something like ValidationError according to the documentation.
